turns.t: Hi, doctor. I've been, oh, what's the word, I've got that pain all over, fibromyalgia, and I'm tired all the time, and I wanted to review my tablets.
Of course. Tell me how the pain and the tiredness have been.
Aching everywhere, mostly my back, shoulders and hips, and heavy tired, I wake up unrefreshed. It's worse when it's cold.
When did it flare up this time?
A few weeks ago? Or longer, it's difficult to say, it creeps up on me.
That's understandable. Any fevers, swollen joints, or rashes?
No. None.
Any weight loss, or night sweats?
No, nothing like that.
Let's go through the tablets.
Amitriptyline, 10 mg at night. Duloxetine, 60 mg once a day, and paracetamol, 1 gram, when I need it.
And are they helping? ~
The amitriptyline helps me sleep. The duloxetine, I'm not sure. ~
Any side effects, dry mouth, nausea, constipation? ~
A dry mouth, and a bit of nausea when I started. That's settled. ~
Any other conditions?
Irritable bowel. And I get low in winter.
Let me check your pulse and blood pressure. ~
Of course. ~
Pulse 70, blood pressure 124 over 78.
All right? ~
Fine. Nothing about the examination or your history suggests a different cause, so I'd say this is a flare of your fibromyalgia.
It's so frustrating. ~
I know. I'd like to arrange a blood test, to check your thyroid, vitamin D and inflammation markers, just to make sure there's nothing else contributing.
Fine. ~
And I'd like to refer you to the pain management programme, which teaches pacing, gentle exercise, and coping strategies.
Does that really help? ~
Yes, evidence shows that regular gentle exercise, like swimming, walking and yoga, helps more than most tablets.
I used to swim. ~
Start with ten minutes, and build slowly. Don't push on bad days. ~
I'll try. ~
I'd like to see you again in six weeks, to see how the plan is going.
Six weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~
